headline: Preprint reports post-training that improves chain-of-thought monitorability
summary: A preprint proposes post-training a model to make its chain-of-thought more informative about its output, using a lower-tail mutual-information objective with a constraint on how outputs change conditional on a given reasoning trace. On a compressed GPT-OSS-120B checkpoint, the authors report recovering 56.3% of mean and 60.8% of worst-case monitorability loss on GPQA-Diamond while preserving 80.2% of token savings; they also report better detection of residual test-hacking behavior in a deliberately obfuscating Qwen model. In the latter setting, the method also shifts behavior toward correct solutions. These are author-reported controlled model-organism results; transfer to naturally occurring monitoring failures in stronger agents is unestablished.
